transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess what brings me in is I’ve just kind of stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. I don’t mean to make it sound too dramatic, but I’m not really going to salsa nights, or church gatherings, and even cooking for the neighbors feels like too much. Sometimes I don’t even want to walk into my shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood, and that’s always been something I loved. I figured maybe I should talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess… it’s been about six months now. I kept telling myself it was just a rough patch or stress, you know, nothing to make a fuss over. But it’s gone on long enough that I’m starting to think it’s more than just a bad week.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before this period started?

Not like I used to, no. I mean… I can still tell those things matter to me, if that makes sense, but the pleasure just isn’t really there. Salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for folks nearby… even going into my shop just to smell the wood, which used to lift me up, feels kind of flat now. I don’t want to sound ungrateful or anything, but it’s been hard to enjoy those things lately.
Have you been having any thoughts about death or wishing you were dead?

I… I don’t want to worry anyone, and I’m not trying to be dramatic. But yes, I have had thoughts like… maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I catch myself thinking my family might be better off without me, which scares me to even say out loud. I know that probably sounds bad… I’m sorry.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or the way you move?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but my energy’s been pretty low. Even if I sit down for a while, or get a full night in bed, my body still feels worn out—like I’ve been framing a roof all day.

And little things… like loading tools into the truck, things I’ve done my whole life, they can feel like too much lately. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, but that’s what it’s been like.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?
I don’t think so… not anything I’ve really noticed, anyway. My clothes seem to fit about the same. I haven’t been weighing myself much, though, so I don’t want to say for sure if that’s okay.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or do you feel restless and can't sit still?

Yeah… I guess so. I mean, I didn’t really want to make a big thing of it, but people at work have noticed.

Some days I’m moving so slow it’s like my boots are full of wet cement—takes me forever just to pick up a board or get going. And then other times I’m not exactly getting anything done, I’m just pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands, like I can’t settle.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yeah, it’s been happening.
Have you been feeling guilty about things or blaming yourself more often than usual?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to sound dramatic or like I’m just feeling sorry for myself, but I keep going back over everything with my wife’s health.

Every appointment, every little change I noticed or maybe didn’t notice… I keep thinking a better husband would’ve caught it sooner, or protected her somehow. I know that may not be fair, but it’s hard not to blame myself.
Have you ever felt this way before, with periods of low mood and loss of interest in activities?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I’ve had rough stretches before, like anyone, I guess, where I wasn’t myself for a while.

But I don’t know if I’d say it was the same as this, or if it counts as what you’re asking. I’m sorry, I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.
Have you experienced any unusual thoughts or heard voices that others couldn't hear?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had my mind run away with me, sure, but not voices or anything like that.

And unusual thoughts… I guess I’m not totally sure what counts as unusual, but I haven’t been hearing things other people don’t hear. I don’t want to answer it wrong, but I don’t think that’s been happening.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t want to say no if I’m just not remembering it right, but I also don’t want to make it sound worse than it was.

There have been times I was down, sure… but more than one period like this, where I felt really low and disconnected from things? I don’t know. I guess I’d need help sorting out what counts.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt similarly low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy, before the six months that brought you here today?

I’m honestly not sure. I know I’ve had some bad patches before, but I don’t know if they were really the same as this.

Before these last six months… I guess I can’t point to a clear period where I felt this low and disconnected in the same way. Maybe there were times I brushed off or just kept working through, but I don’t want to say something that isn’t accurate. Does that make sense?
Have you had an episode like this before in your life where you felt similarly low and disconnected?

I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve had rough times before, sure, but I’m not sure I’d call them an episode like this.

This feels… heavier, I guess. Or maybe I just didn’t pay enough attention back then. I don’t want to overstate it. I can’t think of another time that clearly matches this, if that’s what you’re asking.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for depression before?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve never been formally diagnosed with depression or treated for it before.

I mean, I may have had times where I wasn’t doing great, but I never really went in for it or had anyone tell me that was what it was. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt similarly low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so… not more than one that I can clearly point to.

I’ve had hard stretches, like I said, but I’m not sure they were the same kind of low or being disconnected from things. I don’t want to give you the wrong impression just to have an answer. So, I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure, but I can’t really identify more than one.
Have you experienced an episode of feeling similarly low and disconnected before this six-month period?

I’m not sure I can say yes to that. I’ve had times that were hard, but before this six-month stretch, I don’t remember anything that felt clearly like the same thing.

I don’t want to miss something important, but if you’re asking whether there was another definite episode like this, I don’t think I can point to one.
Have you had any periods of significant improvement in your mood and interest in activities since this six-month period started?

Not really, no… I mean, maybe I’ve had an odd better day here or there, but nothing I’d call a real improvement.

It’s been kind of dragging on for about six months now. I kept telling myself it was just stress or a rough patch, but it’s gone on long enough that it doesn’t really feel like just a bad week anymore, if that makes sense.

Have you had any periods in your life before these six months where you felt similarly low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy, and then got better for a while before feeling this way again?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone, but I can’t honestly point to a time where I was this low and disconnected, then got better, and then it came back like this.

I hope that makes sense… I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t want to say yes if I’m not really sure.
Have you had any previous episodes of depression that were treated and resolved before this current episode started?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve never really had a depression episode that was treated and then went away before this.

I mean, I’ve had rough times, but nothing where I was in treatment for it and it resolved, as far as I can remember. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever felt this low and disconnected before this six-month period and then gotten better on your own?

I’m not really sure I have, no. I mean, I’ve had times where I was stressed or kind of down, but I don’t remember being this low and checked out and then just bouncing back on my own.

If anything happened like that, it wasn’t clear enough that I’d feel right calling it the same thing. Does that make sense?
